sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:14

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:14:1
items.html: He calls the light here by the name interiority, and the vessel by the name exteriority. And the matter of interiority and exteriority is something we must always understand according to the context in which it is spoken of.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:14:2
items.html: The vessels of the World of Assiya are called Ofanim, and the lights that are in the World of Assiya are called Nefesh.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:14:3
items.html: That is, with regard to the ten "comprehensive" Sefirot, which are the five worlds — Adam Kadmon and Atzilut-Beriah-Yetzirah-Assiya — corresponding to Keter-Hochma-Bina, Zeir Anpin, Malchut, in which clothe Yechida, Chaya, Neshama, Ruach, Nefesh: in this regard, all the lights of Assiya are found to be only the phase of Malchut and Nefesh. However, with regard to the particular scope of the World of Assiya itself, all of Nefesh-Ruach-Neshama-Chaya-Yechida are found there, as will be explained further on.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:14:4
items.html:
That is, five Partzufim, and in each and every Partzuf there is a full Nefesh-Ruach-Neshama-Chaya-Yechida; and know that these twenty-five phases necessarily apply in every world by virtue of the emanation of that one degree in which that world is discerned, as written about this in Inner Observation here. Therefore it is necessary to discern, even in the World of Adam Kadmon, five Partzufim, in each of which there are ten Sefirot — Keter-Hochma-Bina, Zeir Anpin, Nukva — each lower than the other, within which the Nefesh-Ruach-Neshama-Chaya-Yechida of that particular Partzuf clothes.
And here you must discern that there are two kinds of ten Sefirot: the first are the ten Sefirot Keter-Hochma-Bina, Zeir Anpin, and Malchut whose stature is equal, meaning that they emerge through a coupling of striking at a single time, that is, from a single phase. And the second are the ten Sefirot Keter-Hochma-Bina, Zeir-Nukva, each lower than the other, meaning that they emerge through five couplings of striking, on account of the successive refinement of the screen, as written above regarding the order of emanation of the five worlds Adam Kadmon and Atzilut-Beriah-Yetzirah-Assiya.
And know that those twenty-five phases that necessarily apply in every world, spoken of in the words of the Rav, refer only to the phase of the ten Sefirot each lower than the other; for those ten Sefirot whose stature is equal are considered only a single Sefira, named after the higher light within that stature (as above, Chapter 9, item 3).

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 3:14:5
items.html: This is a very important piece of knowledge, needed for the understanding of many matters, and one must always remember it. And the first understanding is this: because of this, when some movement or renewal occurs in any world, in even the slightest phase among them, this particular movement causes a renewal in the totality of all the worlds, from the Head of the Line to the end of Assiya, whether for punishment or for kindness — this is exactly like a single person, of whom it is inconceivable that only a small part of one of his limbs should feel pain, or feel pleasure there, without the whole body, from his head to the nails of his feet, feeling it. So too is this matter, and understand it well.
